entries.name: Association québécoise du syndrome de la Tourette (AQST)
entries.description: Quebec-wide French-language non-profit for people with Tourette syndrome (syndrome Gilles de la Tourette) and tic disorders, their families and the professionals who work with them. It runs in-person support groups by region, monthly online groups for parents and caregivers, evenings for adults with TS, activities for youth aged 7 to 17, and information and training.
entries.cost_note: Membership available; group fees not stated.
entries.evidence: Les groupes de soutien ont été créés pour soutenir les parents, proches aidant, adultes et adolescents qui vivent avec le syndrome Gilles de la Tourette (SGT).
entries.notes: Mostly French; there is an English link on the site. Group schedules are posted on its Facebook page.

entries.name: Tourette OCD Alberta Network (University of Calgary)
entries.description: University of Calgary network that improves access to care for children and adults with Tourette syndrome, tic disorders and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). It offers free care navigation, online peer group discussions for parents moderated by a psychologist, educational outreach to schools, webinars, and a directory of health professionals by province.
entries.cost_note: All Canadians are eligible for its free services.
entries.evidence: Our mission is to improve access to care for people with Tourette Syndrome and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder province wide.
entries.notes: Says all Canadians are eligible for its free services, so a reviewer may prefer it as a national entry. Parent peer groups run weekly for five weeks, capped at 15 participants. The contact email on the page is a named staff member's, so it is left out.

entries.name: Foothills Academy School
entries.description: Calgary designated special education private school for students in grades 3 to 12 who have diagnosed learning disabilities such as dyslexia. Its society also runs year-round community services for people of all ages with learning disabilities and/or ADHD.
entries.cost_note: Private school; many students attend with help from its bursary program.
entries.evidence: Foothills Academy School is a Designated Special Education Private School for students in grades 3 to 12, all of whom have diagnosed Learning Disabilities (such as Dyslexia).
entries.notes: Students must have a diagnosed learning disability. Grades 3 to 12 is roughly ages 8 to 18.

entries.name: Psycho-educational Assessments (Foothills Academy Estelle Siebens Community Services)
entries.description: Psycho-educational assessments in Calgary for children aged 6 and up, teens and adults, to identify learning disabilities such as dyslexia, ADHD and related needs, done by registered psychologists and supervised trainees. The same community services centre also offers counselling, small groups, camps and parent education for people with learning disabilities and/or ADHD.
entries.cost_note: Flat rate $2475 per assessment from January 2026; may be covered by benefit plans; fee reduction by application.
entries.evidence: The Estelle Siebens Community Services centre assists individuals of all ages with Learning Disabilities and/or ADHD in the Calgary community and well beyond.
entries.notes: Full assessments take about six to eight weeks and give a 20 to 30 page report. Staff do not do autism assessments. Fee reduction bursaries are mainly for children and teens.

entries.name: International Dyslexia Association Ontario Branch (IDA Ontario)
entries.description: Ontario non-profit branch of the International Dyslexia Association for families, educators and people with dyslexia. It runs a dyslexia infoline, webinars and in-person events for parents, at-home and at-school resources, structured literacy training for educators, and advocacy.
entries.cost_note: Some webinars and events have fees; members get special rates.
entries.evidence: IDA Ontario offers webinars, events, resources, and volunteer opportunities to help families learn, connect, and advocate for their children.
entries.notes: The phone line is not monitored (leave a message); the site recommends the contact form. Mailing address is a PO box in Hamilton.

entries.name: Institut des troubles d'apprentissage (Institut TA)
entries.description: Quebec's French-language learning disabilities organisation for people with learning disabilities (troubles d'apprentissage), such as dyslexia (dyslexie), and their parents and teachers. It offers a resource library, at-home reading, writing and math activities for parents, parent days, conferences and training, and answers questions with support and referrals.
entries.cost_note: Many resources free online; conferences and training may have fees.
entries.evidence: L’endroit pour trouver des réponses à vos questions, du soutien et des références pour tout ce qui est en lien direct avec les difficultés d’apprentissage ou les troubles d’apprentissage!
entries.notes: French only; LDAC lists it as the Quebec member association (formerly AQETA), with phone 514-847-1324 and an office at 1940 Henri-Bourassa Blvd. East, Montreal. Its own contact page gives only email and hours (8:30 to 4:30, Monday to Friday).

entries.name: LD Edmonton (Learning Disabilities Association of Edmonton)
entries.description: Edmonton chapter of the Learning Disabilities Association of Alberta for children, youth and adults with learning disabilities and/or ADHD. It runs a child social skills program, a summer day camp, social groups, information sessions and parent support groups, and helps with advocacy.
entries.cost_note: Not stated on the home page.
entries.evidence: Our goal at LDEdmonton is to provide a safe environment for individuals with LD and/or ADHD to learn how to better interpret and more effectively maneuver social interactions.
entries.notes: Mailing address only (Box 213 Edmonton Main). Program pages (Child Social Skills Program, Camp Abilities, Parent Support Groups) are linked from the home page.

entries.name: Learning Disabilities Association of Chatham-Kent (LDAC-K)
entries.description: Chatham-Kent charity for children, youth and adults with learning disabilities, affiliated with LDAO and LDAC. It runs one-to-one tutoring for elementary school children, the B.E.S.T. social skills program, an executive functioning skills group, a full-week summer camp, and advocacy.
entries.cost_note: Tutoring $15/hour ($450 for 30 hours of tutoring, assessments and reports).
entries.evidence: Our Tutoring Program is a unique one-to-one, after-school and summer program offered to children of elementary school age.
entries.notes: Tutoring runs in 15-week terms (September to January, February to June) plus summer blocks; registration is confirmed only after payment and a call from staff.

entries.name: Learning Disabilities Association of Durham Region (LDADR)
entries.description: Volunteer-run Durham Region chapter of LDAO for people with learning disabilities and ADHD and their families. Advocacy advisors give phone and in-person support and can help parents at school IPRC and IEP meetings, and a resource facilitator answers questions about LDs, ADHD and local supports.
entries.cost_note: Resource facilitation and speaker series free for all; advocacy support is for members.
entries.evidence: Our advocacy team members will provide telephone and in person support. They are also available to assist parents at the school IPRC/IEP meetings.
entries.notes: The programs page still says sessions are on hold (it mentions fall 2022), so group programs may not be running; advocacy and resource facilitation are listed as current. Mailing address only (P.O. Box 346, Pickering).

entries.name: Learning Disabilities Association London Region (LDALR)
entries.description: London, Ontario charity for children, youth and families affected by learning disabilities and ADHD. It offers academic tutoring, reading, writing and executive functioning programs, a pathways-to-post-secondary program, summer camps, and parent services such as consultations, school advocacy, advocacy workshops and parent groups.
entries.cost_note: Programs have fees; staff can discuss reducing or waiving fees at intake.
entries.evidence: We offer a multitude of parent services that include consultations, documentation analysis, school advocacy, parent advocacy workshops, and parent groups.
entries.notes: New clients start with a registration form, then staff call to discuss needs. Phone is extension 5.

entries.name: Learning Disabilities Association of Windsor-Essex County (LDAWE)
entries.description: Windsor-Essex charity that provides information, support and programs for children, youth and adults with learning disabilities, ADHD and associated disorders. Services include a parent support group, Thrive coaching, employment services, scholarships and resources on LDs and ADHD.
entries.cost_note: Not stated on the home page.
entries.evidence: Information, support and programs to help children, youth and adults with learning disabilities.
entries.notes: Office open Monday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., on the Maryvale campus.

entries.name: Learning Disabilities Association of Alberta (LDAA)
entries.description: Alberta's provincial association for people with learning disabilities, including dyslexia, and their families, educators and adults with LDs. It runs online webinar and course series for parents and adults, a Learner's Licence Prep Kit, scholarships and awards, and literacy courses for educators and tutors.
entries.cost_note: Courses and webinars require registration; fees not listed on the pages checked.
entries.evidence: Since 1968, we have provided assistance and resources to Alberta families, educators, and adults who rely on LDAA for information, education, and help in finding what they need to navigate learning disabilities.
entries.notes: Mailing address is a PO box (Box 30524, Chinook P.O., Calgary). Local programs are run by the LD Edmonton chapter and the LD-ADHD Network in Calgary.

entries.name: LDABC The Learning Curve (Learning Disabilities Association, South Vancouver Island Chapter)
entries.description: Victoria non-profit, the South Vancouver Island chapter of the Learning Disabilities Association of BC, for children and youth with learning disabilities or other learning and behaviour challenges, including those who struggle with reading and writing. It offers one-on-one academic skills and reading and writing tutoring, a B.C.-wide online reading program, summer writing workshops, and workshops for parents and caregivers.
entries.cost_note: Online reading program $50/month; summer writing workshop $250; parent workshops about $20. Financial assistance may be available.
entries.evidence: LDABC The Learning Curve supports families and educates and advocates for children and youth experiencing learning and/or behavioral challenges.
entries.notes: Children do not need a learning disability assessment to join the reading and writing program. Intake can take 4 to 6 weeks at busy times. The online reading program is open across B.C.

entries.name: Learning Disabilities Association of Manitoba (LDAM)
entries.description: Winnipeg-based charity for Manitobans of all ages with learning disabilities, including dyslexia, dyscalculia and dysgraphia, and/or ADHD. It offers counselling, one-on-one tutoring for struggling readers, social skills groups, help with assessment and diagnosis, and support for parents and caregivers.
entries.cost_note: Counselling $65 per 50-minute session, sliding scale available; most programs low or no cost.
entries.evidence: Whether you're seeking support for yourself, your child, or a student you teach, the Learning Disabilities Association of Manitoba is here. Programs, counselling, and community for all ages.
entries.notes: Counselling can be booked online. Office hours Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. LDAC still lists the old address (617 Erin Street); the association's own site says 609 Erin Street.

entries.name: Learning Disabilities Association of New Brunswick (LDANB-TAANB)
entries.description: Bilingual provincial association in Fredericton for people with learning disabilities, including dyslexia, and their families. It runs the Barton Tutoring Program for reading and spelling, offers information and advocacy, and provides the Screening for Success tool and training for screening adults who may have a learning disability.
entries.cost_note: Tutoring fees not listed; contact the association.
entries.evidence: establish accurate information regarding learning disabilities assist families, adults with LD, and professionals speak as a provincial authority on learning disabilities
entries.notes: Site is in English and French. Barton tutoring details are given on request (the home page says to contact LDANB-TAANB).

entries.name: Learning Disabilities Association of Newfoundland and Labrador (LDANL)
entries.description: St. John's non-profit for children, youth and adults with learning disabilities such as dyslexia and dyscalculia, and ADHD. It offers one-on-one reading and math tutoring, screening, an adult literacy project, assistive technology support, tutoring support for rural and low-income families, and programs for newcomers and parents.
entries.cost_note: Reading tutoring $29 per 55-minute one-on-one session; some funded programs are free for eligible learners.
entries.address: 136 Crosbie Road (The Viking Building), 4th floor, Suite 400
entries.evidence: We help people who struggle with Dyslexia, Dyscalculia, ADHD and more!
entries.notes: Reading tutoring is open to anyone with reading difficulties, whatever the cause. Funded programs (rural and low-income tutoring, adult literacy) have their own eligibility.

entries.name: Learning Disabilities Association of Ontario (LDAO)
entries.description: Ontario's provincial charity for children, youth and adults with learning disabilities (LDs) and/or ADHD, and their families. It offers information on LDs, online courses and workshops, scholarships and bursaries, and advocacy, and links people to local LDA chapters that run tutoring, social skills and peer support programs.
entries.cost_note: Free resources for educators; LD@learning online courses are paid.
entries.evidence: LDAO serves as a provincial leader and partner in supporting individuals with learning disabilities and their families
entries.notes: The provincial office mainly provides information, courses and advocacy; hands-on programs are run by the 11 local chapters. Email contact is through a web form on the contact page.

entries.name: Learning Disabilities Association of Saskatchewan (LDAS)
entries.description: Saskatchewan association with local branches for neurodivergent people, especially those with learning disabilities such as reading and math challenges, and ADHD. It offers psychoeducational assessments, academic tutoring and strategy programs, ADHD coaching, an adult academic program, employability coaching, a homework club, a summer day camp and workshops.
entries.cost_note: Psychoeducational assessment $2600; ICT funding for some adults aged 18 to 65.
entries.evidence: Here at the Learning Disabilities Association of Saskatchewan (LDAS), we champion individuals who are neurodivergent – particularly those with ADHD, and math and reading challenges.
entries.notes: Branch phone numbers are not printed on the pages fetched (LDAC lists (306) 652-4114 for the Saskatoon office). ICT funding is for unemployed or underemployed adults aged 18 to 65; call a local branch to check eligibility.

entries.name: Institute for Stuttering Treatment and Research (ISTAR), University of Alberta
entries.description: Not-for-profit stuttering clinic of the University of Alberta, with offices in Edmonton and Calgary, offering specialized treatment for children, teens and adults who stutter, and other communication help through its Communication Improvement Program. Families apply directly for an assessment, and a donor-funded fund can reduce fees for those in financial need.
entries.cost_note: Speech therapy fees apply; the ISTAR Client Assistance Program (ICAP) Fund gives income-based subsidies.
entries.evidence: We offer specialized treatment to children, teens and adults who stutter.
entries.notes: Calgary office phone 403-201-7285. Application forms for adults and teens are on the treatment options page.

entries.name: Children's Speech Therapy Program (Speech and Stuttering Institute)
entries.description: Speech therapy for children aged 2 and up whose main challenge is saying words clearly, including childhood apraxia of speech (CAS), childhood dysarthria, motor speech delay and other speech sound disorders. Therapy is family-centred, uses principles of motor learning, and is offered in person in Toronto or virtually across Ontario.
entries.cost_note: Fee-based; subsidy fund available for families in financial need.
entries.evidence: Our SLPs are experienced and well-equipped to help with all of them, including: Articulation delay or disorder Phonological delay or disorder Childhood Apraxia of Speech (CAS)
entries.notes: No doctor's referral needed. The site says ages 2+; older children may also be seen, so check with the clinic.

entries.name: Stuttering Therapy Programs (Speech and Stuttering Institute)
entries.description: Non-profit Toronto clinic offering assessment and therapy for people who stutter: a Preschool Fluency Program, a School Age Fluency Program, and Adult and Teen Stuttering Therapy Programs. No referral is needed, and virtual therapy is available anywhere in Ontario.
entries.cost_note: Fees below Ontario SLP guidelines; the Bob Kroll Subsidy Fund can reduce fees for families in financial need.
entries.evidence: SSI is a non-profit organization in Toronto, offering speech therapy to children and adults with speech and stuttering challenges.
entries.notes: Self-referral; in-person services at the Toronto clinic and tele-practice across Ontario. It is designated by the Ontario Ministry of Children, Community and Social Services as a training centre for motor speech and stuttering therapies.

entries.name: Down Syndrome Society of British Columbia (Down Syndrome BC)
entries.description: Province-wide group of parents, guardians, caregivers and self-advocates in British Columbia who support people with Down syndrome. It advocates and shares information on inclusive education, health care and early intervention, and connects families with lived experience across B.C.
entries.cost_note: Not stated.
entries.evidence: We will forge connections across our province-wide community so that families and individuals with lived experience (the real experts!) can guide each other.
entries.notes: Mainly advocacy and family-to-family connection; local programs are run by regional societies (Lower Mainland, Greater Victoria, Fraser Valley and others).

entries.name: Down Syndrome Association of the National Capital Region (DSANCR)
entries.description: Bilingual Ottawa-area non-profit for people with Down syndrome and their families at every stage of life. It offers support, resources, advocacy and education, and runs programs such as a family playgroup for babies and children 12 and under and a free weekly craft club for adults 21 and over.
entries.cost_note: Some programs listed as free; others not stated.
entries.evidence: Our mission is to provide support, resources, and opportunities that empower individuals and their families at every stage of life.
entries.notes: Programs are listed on its events calendar in English and French. Age ranges are for the family playgroup; adult clubs are for ages 21 and over.

entries.name: Down Syndrome Association of Ontario (DSAO)
entries.description: Charitable federation of local Down syndrome associations across Ontario that works for people with Down syndrome and their families. It raises awareness, advocates on health care, education and social services, promotes best practices and coordinates government relations, and links families to their local association.
entries.cost_note: Not stated.
entries.evidence: Together, we coordinate the efforts to raise awareness, educate, and encourage the inclusion of people with Down syndrome and their families across Ontario.
entries.notes: Provincial umbrella body; direct programs are run by local associations (Toronto, Ottawa, Hamilton, Peel, York and others). A second number, 905-439-6644, is also listed.

entries.name: Down Syndrome Association of Toronto (DSAT)
entries.description: Toronto non-profit charity for people with Down syndrome and their families throughout the GTA. It runs programs and social events such as Dance Rock dances, shares resources, advocates and promotes inclusion.
entries.cost_note: Some events ticketed; support persons get a free ticket.
entries.evidence: Our mission is to support and empower individuals with Down Syndrome and their families throughout the GTA.
entries.notes: Events need registration in advance; guests are expected to come without needing staff support (a support person may come along).

entries.name: Down Syndrome Resource Foundation (DSRF)
entries.description: Burnaby, B.C. charity for people with Down syndrome and their families, offering individualized educational programs, therapy and health services, information resources and social connections. It runs group education and recreation programs for youth and adults and supports students with Down syndrome and other intellectual disabilities.
entries.cost_note: Program fees not shown on the pages checked.
entries.evidence: Our mission is to support people with Down syndrome and their families with specialized education and therapy services, information resources, and rich social connections so that each person can flourish in their own right.
entries.notes: Toll-free in Canada 1-888-464-DSRF. Contact is by phone or the web form.

entries.name: Edmonton Down Syndrome Society (EDSS)
entries.description: Edmonton society for people with Down syndrome and their families, with programs, information, resources and peer-to-peer support. It offers speech-language, occupational, behavioural and physiotherapy services, an adult day program, a free drop-in for young children, sports, dance and musical theatre programs.
entries.cost_note: Program pricing for members (membership required); Monday morning drop-in for little ones is free.
entries.evidence: The Edmonton Down Syndrome Society (EDSS) is committed to supporting people with Down syndrome and their families, through programming, information, resources and connecting members with peer to peer support.
entries.notes: A valid EDSS membership is needed for advertised program prices; non-member pricing on request. Program emails on the site are a named staff member's.

entries.name: Greater Moncton Down Syndrome Society (GMDSS)
entries.description: Parent-founded charity supporting people with Down syndrome and their families in southeastern New Brunswick. It offers a family support network, home and hospital visits to new families, new parent information, social events, information workshops and a camp bursary.
entries.cost_note: Not stated.
entries.evidence: GMDSS is aware of the isolating effects a diagnosis of Down Syndrome can bring to a family, GMDSS also offers home and hospital visits to any family looking for support and the answers to their many questions.
entries.notes: The email is the society's own Gmail address. The camp bursary helps with camp costs (see its Camp Bursary page).

entries.name: Halifax NS Down Syndrome Society (HNSDSS)
entries.description: Volunteer non-profit that is a resource for people with Down syndrome and their families across Nova Scotia. It supports new parents, including home visits on request, and runs educational workshops, social programs such as Friday Night Socials and Team Possibles, and an annual Maritime Down syndrome family camp.
entries.cost_note: Not stated.
entries.evidence: Halifax NS Down Syndrome Society provides support and information to new families. On request members of our society can make a visit to your home.
entries.notes: Formerly the Nova Scotia Down Syndrome Society; it also has a private Facebook group for Nova Scotia families.

entries.name: Lower Mainland Down Syndrome Society (LMDSS)
entries.description: Surrey-based society for people with Down syndrome and their families in B.C.'s Lower Mainland. It offers new parent information packages in 10 languages, affordable classes for members and non-members, a summer camp, advice and help with forms and services.
entries.cost_note: Classes described as affordable; prices not on the home page.
entries.evidence: Whether you need a form, some advice, services, or even just a friendly ear, the Lower Mainland Down Syndrome Society is here for you, your family, and your child.
entries.notes: New parent packages are available in 10 languages, useful for newcomer families.

entries.name: Manitoba Down Syndrome Society (MDSS)
entries.description: Winnipeg-based society for people with Down syndrome and their families across Manitoba, at every stage of life. It welcomes new families, runs peer groups and events, an Active Youth sport program, social clubs for young adults, education for families, and a fund for community programs outside Winnipeg.
entries.cost_note: Program fees with accessible pricing for low-income members (based on LICO-AT).
entries.evidence: The Manitoba Down Syndrome Society (MDSS) provides a diverse range of programs designed to support individuals and families at every stage of their lives.
entries.notes: The site writes its email address in an obfuscated form (info at manitobadownsyndromesociety dot com), so it is left out. Social clubs meet twice a month, September to June.

entries.name: Newfoundland & Labrador Down Syndrome Society (NLDSS)
entries.description: Volunteer non-profit of family and friends in Newfoundland and Labrador for children, youth and adults with Down syndrome. It raises awareness and works for access to education, health care and employment, with free membership for families.
entries.cost_note: Membership is free.
entries.address: 21 Pippy Place, St. John’s, NL, A1B 3X2
entries.evidence: Newfoundland and Labrador Down syndrome Society is a volunteer non-profit organization of family and friends dedicated to ensuring a fulfilling quality of life for children, youth and adults with Down syndrome.
entries.notes: The newest posts seen on the home page are about 2024 events, so a reviewer may want to confirm it is still active. The email is the society's own Gmail address.

entries.name: Regroupement pour la Trisomie 21 (RT21)
entries.description: Montreal French-language community organisation for people with Down syndrome (trisomie 21) and their families. It offers day programs, respite for family caregivers, specialised services, and individual and group support, including help with school inclusion and family activities.
entries.cost_note: Not stated on the home page.
entries.address: 1A-3250 boulevard Saint-Joseph Est, Montréal, Québec H1Y 3G2
entries.evidence: Le RT21 est un organisme communautaire dédié à l’accompagnement des personnes ayant une trisomie 21 et de leurs familles.
entries.notes: French-language site. Other Quebec regional associations (Sherbrooke, Lanaudière) are listed on the CDSS map.

entries.name: Saskatchewan Down Syndrome Society (SDSS)
entries.description: Parent-founded Saskatchewan society for children and adults with Down syndrome and their families. It educates, advocates and gives practical support, and provides resources for parents, caregivers, educators and professionals.
entries.cost_note: Not stated.
entries.evidence: We educate, advocate and practically support individuals with Down syndrome, their families and their communities.
entries.notes: The email is the society's own Gmail address. The site also lists a mailing address in Dalmeny, SK.

entries.name: Ups & Downs - Calgary Down Syndrome Association
entries.description: Calgary charity for people with Down syndrome and their parents, families and friends. It runs more than 70 programs a year, including events and workshops for children, youth and adults, a teen and young adult conference, visiting parents for new and expecting families, and a members' online group.
entries.cost_note: Membership available; fees not stated on the home page.
entries.evidence: If you are a new or expecting parent, are new to the Calgary area, or are looking to connect with other parents, Ups and Downs is here for you.
entries.notes: New and expecting parents can ask to be connected with a visiting parent.

entries.name: Support Groups (Tourette Canada)
entries.description: Weekly and monthly online support groups across Canada for people with Tourette syndrome and tic disorders and their families. Groups include Moms of Children with Tourette Syndrome, Adults with Tourette Syndrome, a Youth Hangout for ages 13 to 18, and a monthly general group open to anyone with Tourette, parents and caregivers.
entries.cost_note: Registration required; no fee mentioned.
entries.evidence: Anyone and everyone across Canada is welcome (people with tourette, caregivers, parents, any age)
entries.notes: Moms group meets Mondays, adults Tuesdays, youth Wednesdays (evenings Eastern time); the general group meets every third Tuesday. Email admin@tourette.ca for the Zoom link.

entries.name: Tourette Canada
entries.description: National volunteer-based charity for children, adults and families living with Tourette syndrome (TS) and other tic disorders. It offers virtual support groups, educational webinars, in-service presentations for schools and professionals, an information package and handbooks for families and educators.
entries.cost_note: Handbooks are sold in its store; membership and other costs not stated.
entries.evidence: Our programs are structured to promote broad-based national awareness and understanding of Tourette Syndrome; educate the community about the Syndrome and support meaningful engagement between children, adults and families living with Tourette
entries.notes: Home office in Brampton, Ontario (905-673-2255), open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern. It has a strategic partnership with the Tourette OCD Alberta Network.

entries.name: Dyslexia Compass (Dyslexia Canada)
entries.description: Free family support program from Dyslexia Canada, a national charity, for parents and caregivers of children with dyslexia anywhere in Canada. Volunteer supporters with lived experience guide families by email, phone or virtual meeting through finding out whether a child has dyslexia, getting help at school and finding a tutor.
entries.cost_note: Free family support program.
entries.evidence: Dyslexia Compass is Dyslexia Canada’s free family support program for parents and caregivers of children with dyslexia.
entries.notes: Families start with an intake form on the page and are matched with a team member. Dyslexia Canada also publishes a free parent handbook and provincial progress reports.

entries.name: Support Groups (Canadian Stuttering Association)
entries.description: Peer support groups for people who stutter, run with the Canadian Stuttering Association. They include online groups for youth, teens, parents, university and college students and the Prairies, and in-person regional groups in Edmonton, Vancouver, Mount Pearl (NL), Guelph, Mississauga, Ottawa and Toronto, plus an online Halton group.
entries.cost_note: Not stated.
entries.evidence: Online Support Group for Youth Who Stutter Online Teen Support Group Parents Online Support Group Prairie Online Support Group University-College Student Online Support Group
entries.notes: Each group has its own contact on the CSA site. The Mount Pearl group is run by the Newfoundland and Labrador Stuttering Association (NLSA).

entries.name: Canadian Stuttering Association (CSA)
entries.description: National volunteer-driven charity for people who stutter, their families and allies. It raises awareness of stuttering, runs support groups and events, and gives information on finding speech therapy for preschoolers, school-age children, teens and adults, plus pages for parents and youth.
entries.cost_note: Not stated.
entries.evidence: promotes awareness and understanding of stuttering and provides support and resources for people who stutter, their families and allies
entries.notes: Toronto phone 416-840-5169. Lists local and online support groups on a separate page.

entries.name: Canadian Down Syndrome Society (CDSS)
entries.description: National charity for people with Down syndrome (trisomy 21) and their parents and families across Canada. It offers a resource hub on all aspects of living with Down syndrome, person-centred support and connections to services, a network of local Down syndrome groups, and advocacy on health, inclusive education and employment.
entries.cost_note: Information and support line; no fees mentioned.
entries.evidence: CDSS supports self-advocates, parents and families through all stages of life.
entries.notes: Its About page has a map of local Down syndrome associations and community groups by province. Local and international phone +01-403-270-8500.
